## Histogram features · centres and boundaries {#l2-histogram-rules .compact}

```{=html}
<div data-module="histogram-features" class="histogram-features"></div>
```

<p class="small-note">Equal-width bars touch. Label both axes and use a consistent scale. A relative frequency histogram uses <strong>relative frequency</strong> on the vertical axis.</p>

::: notes
Use the discrete/continuous buttons to compare where numbers belong. Discrete example x=1,2,3,4 with frequencies 2,5,4,1: unit-width bars have boundaries 0.5,1.5,…,4.5, with numbers 1,2,3,4 centred below the bars. Annotate the half-column lead-in between the vertical axis at 0 and first boundary 0.5. This is a leading space, not a gap between adjacent bars.

Continuous example uses equal-width intervals 0≤t<1,1≤t<2,2≤t<3,3≤t<4. Labels 0,1,2,3,4 mark boundaries. Keep a half-column display gap between the vertical axis and the boundary labelled 0, even though the first class starts at 0. The small horizontal-axis break marks this leading display space. Class boundaries and widths remain unchanged. Frequency is on the vertical axis; relative frequency is used for Example 3.8.

For an ordinary-frequency polygon, plot at each value or class centre and join adjacent points, returning to zero one class before and after. Cumulative polygons will instead use upper class boundaries. No unequal-width frequency-density treatment is needed here.
:::
